finding: Partial proof of item (3) on the actual idèle class group of every number field, not yet an identification with the completed middle action. For continuous compactly supported φ and continuous input ψ, the two complex integrands φ(g)ψ(g⁻¹x) and φ(x/y)ψ(y) are both integrable at each x and have equal integrals against the same class Haar. If ψ is in the pointwise χ-isotype for inverse-left translation by the actual norm-one subgroup, the kernel integral retains that equivariance. This works without restricting the field or χ, rescaling Haar, or extending the operator by zero. Topological support at norm >1 gives pointwise diagonal vanishing; support at norm >1+ε gives vanishing throughout |x|_F≤(1+ε)|y|_F, including its boundary. This does not make any trace or spectral comparison. The accepted rational-radial convolution in Theorems.RationalRadialHilbertConvolution is over ℚ in the trivial isotype on a specific radial model, and does not establish the general completed-action identification.
retry: Identify the actual completed W_I^{s,2} norm-one isotype, with the source weight and measure, with a weighted L² isotype, and prove density of its continuous source tests there and agreement of the bounded inverse-left regularization with the test integral. Then use unweighted L² integrability of the compact kernel and the lower bound on the symmetric-base weight to pass to the Haar kernel representative on the same completed isotype (including s=0). See the handoff for the pointwise estimate and the remaining almost-everywhere identification step.
